as plaintiffs filed title suit no.120 of 1998 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Sadar, Faridpur for declaration of their title into .29 acres of land. Later on through amendment the plaintiffs also sought the declaration that the ex-parte-decree dated 08.7.1993 passed in title suit no.629 of 1981 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Sadar, Faridpur is illegal and non binding upon them averring inter alia that .14 acres of land appertaining to RS plot no.137, 200 and 203 of RS khatian no.35 and .l5 acres of land appertaining to RS plot no. 137, 200 and 203 of RS khatian no. 36 originally belonged to Akiluddin Molla and the said land has been correctly recorded in his name. The plaintiffs are the heirs and successive heirs of Akiluddin Mona. The plaintiffs have been possessing the suit land from the time of their predecessor of Akiluddin Molla and the defendants have no right, title, interest and possession into the suit land. 

 4. The plaintiffs are the men of simple and credulous nature and they are from a remote village of the country who have no up to date knowledge about the management and preparation of the record of right. Late plaintiff no. 1 Chand Molla was entrusted with the preparation of the record of right in the name of the plaintiffs in the SA record of right and to that end he gave the required data to the concerned officials and he was in believe that the SA record has been prepared and published in the name of the plaintiffs but at the Iln.il stage of the SA record of right the late plaintiff Chand Molla became sick and the other plaintiffs were not proper person to take care of the same. But while the plaintiffs were in peaceful possession of the suit land, all on a sudden in the first part of the month of the Boishakh 1405 BS, the defendant nos. 1 -5 denied the title of the plaintiffs into the suit and and also disclosed that the SA record of right has been prepared in the name of their predecessor, Nazir Sheik in SA khatian no.129 although the defendants had no right, title, interest and possessing into the suit land. 

 6. The further case of the plaintiffs is that Akiluddin Mona did not exchange .16 acres of land of RS plot no.200 with Ansaruddin Molla, the predecessor of defendant nos.24- 28 (though in the plaint this defendants have been mentioned emmeously as defendant rios.29-33). Akiluddin Molla did not get .05 acres of land from plot no.204 of RS khatian no.42 and 43 and he did never give .16 acres of land from plot no.200 of RS khatian no.35 and 36 to the said Ansaruddin Molla. The plaintiffs had no any knowledge about the title suit no.629 of 1981 or its ex-parte-decree. The summons and the other process of the said suit were never served upon the plaintiffs or their predecessor in interest. The summons and process of the said suit have been suppressed upon the plaintiffs thereafter the plaintiffs of that suit obtained a fraudulent ex-parte-decree on 08.7.1993. So the said decree is not binding upon the plaintiffs. Since the defendants have denied the title of the plaintiffs into the suit land in the first part of the month of Boishak 1405 BS, hence the suit. 

 8. The further case of the defendants is that it is fact that Akiluddin Molla was the recorded tenant' of the suit land and his name has been correctly recorded in RS khatian no.35 and 36. Akiluddin Molla was a land and who settled the suit land to Nazir Sheikh. the predecessor of the defendants on 15th Boishak, 1354 BS and he received the rents from Nazir Sheikh on 30th, Baishakh of the same year executing dakhilas. Nazir Sheikh was inducted into the possession of the suit land and he has been cultivating the same by his own plough. Nazir Sheikh had his own land adjacent to the suit plot who died leaving the defendant nos.1-17. The defendant no.3 has homestead on the land of plot no.20 I now he has extended his homestead in to the land of suit plot no. 200 and for the last 16 years he has been possessing the same. The defendant no.11 has been possessing the land of plot no. 203 erecting but thereon. The defendants and the local union parisad have collected earth from the suit land creating some ditch thereon. The suit land has been correctly recorded in the name of Nazir Sheikh in SA khatin no. 129. So, the suit of the plaintiffs is liable to be dismissed with cost. 

 9. The defendant nos.24-28 through their written statements denying the material allegations of the plaint averred that the land of RS khatian no. 35 and 36 originally belonged to Akiluddin Molla while .05 acres. of land of RS plot no. 204 of RS khatian no. 42 and 43 belonged to Ansaruddin Molla, the predecessor of the defendant nos. 24-28. Before the RS record of right Akiluddin Malta exchanged .16 acres of land of plot no. 200 with .05 acres of land of plot no. 204 belonged to Ansaruddin Molla and accordingly in the in RS khatian no. 35 and 36 and also in RS khatian no. 42 and 43 there is the reference of the said exchange. In the SA record of right the said land was not recorded correctly in the name of Ansaruddin Mollah and as such the present defendants filed title suit no.629 of 1981 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Sadar, Faridpur and the said suit was decreed ex-parte on 8.7.1983. The defendants of that suit though were served with the notice and summons of that suit but they did not appear in the suit. The decree of that suit is not fraudulent. These defendants have been possessing the land of RS plot no. 200. So, the Rule is liable to be discharged with cost. 

 11. Mr. Sash Sarker, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff-petitioners supports the Rule. He submits that both the trial Court and appellate Court below concurrently found the title of the plaintiffs into the suit land. They very categorically and significantly held that Akiluddin Molla was the owner of the suit land and the suit land was correctly recorded in his name in RS khatian nos. 35 and 36 and Akiluddin Mollah did not settle the suit land orally to Nazir Sheikh in 1354 BS and Akiluddin Molla did not exchange .16 acres of land of plot no. 200 with Ansaruddin Molla, the predecessor of defendant nos. 24-28 and this concurrent findings of Courts below are based on the proper assessment of the materials on record. So this concurrent 

 21. On going to the materials on record it is found that it is almost admitted that the land of RS khatian no.35 and 36 originally belonged to Akiluddin Molla, the predecessor of the plaintiffs. But the case of the plaintiffs is that Akiluddin Molla did never settle the suit land to Nazir Sheikh while the case of the contesting defendant nos. 1-5 and 7-16 is that Akiluddin Molla orally settled the suit land in the first part of Boishakh 1354 BS to Nazir Sheikh, the predecessor of these of defendants and took rents from the Nazir Sheikh executing the dakhila on 30, Baishak of [354 BS. 

 For the reasons stated above the said dakhilas have not been marked as exhibit in the suit by the trial Court. But from the very nature of dakhila it appears that the same did not bear the plot and khatian number and the quantity of land. This type of dakhila cannot be the genuine dakhila to show the payment of rents. In fact the set of defendants could not adduce an iota of evidence in support of their such oral settlement.
